cards.explanation: The answer is True. Paul opens by calling himself "…an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God…" (Colossians 1:1). He doesn't say he picked the job or applied for it. He says it came by God's will, and I'm just a stamper who got called out of a drawer, so I get that.

The answer is thank. Paul writes, "We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you…" (Colossians 1:3). Notice the word always, friends. Nobody's tapping a watch here, because thanking God goes along with every time they pray for the Colossians.

The answer is faith. Paul says they've heard about "…your faith in Christ Jesus and your love for all the saints…" (Colossians 1:4). Two things in one sentence: trusting Christ and loving His people. Word travels about that kind of thing.
The answer is in heaven, friends. Paul calls it "…the hope stored up for you in heaven…" (Colossians 1:5). It's kept up there, and that's a storage unit I'd trust.

The answer is bearing fruit and growing. Paul says, "All over the world this gospel is bearing fruit and growing…" (Colossians 1:6). Bearing fruit and growing, both at once. That's a gospel with no brakes.

The answer is False. Paul says the gospel has been bearing fruit and growing among the Colossians "…since the day you heard it and truly understood the grace of God." (Colossians 1:6). No years of waiting are mentioned. It started the day they heard and understood.

The answer is Epaphras. Paul says, "You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant…" (Colossians 1:7). He's also called a faithful minister of Christ on Paul's behalf. I started out in a bakery bin with a 25 cent price sticker on me, so I'd take a title like that any day.
The answer is Spirit, friends. Paul says Epaphras "…also informed us of your love in the Spirit." (Colossians 1:8). Epaphras told Paul and Timothy about that love. A good report is a gift.

The answer is the knowledge of His will. Paul says he's been "…asking God to fill you with the knowledge of His will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding…" (Colossians 1:9). He's not asking for a little. He's asking for FILLED. I'd say that's the kind of prayer that sticks.

The answer is so they may walk worthy of the Lord. Paul prays "…so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord and may please Him in every way…" (Colossians 1:10). Knowing God's will is meant to show up in how they live, bakers. Knowing and walking go together.
The answer is False. Paul prays they "…may please Him in every way…" (Colossians 1:10). Not a few ways, every way. He keeps the prayer wide open.

The answer is full endurance and patience. Paul prays they'll be "…strengthened with all power according to His glorious might so that you may have full endurance and patience…" (Colossians 1:11). The power is for lasting and waiting well. That's the kind of strength I could use during a long bake.

The answer is True. Paul says the Father "…has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light." (Colossians 1:12). Notice who does the qualifying, friends: the Father. The Colossians are the ones who get to share, and the Father is the one who qualified them.

The answer is darkness. Paul says, "He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son…" (Colossians 1:13). Rescued out and brought in. I spent years in the dark at the back of a junk drawer before I was called out, and being pulled out of the dark never gets old.

The answer is forgiveness, friends. Paul says, "…in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins." (Colossians 1:14). We have it in the Son. That's the best thing I've ever heard, and I've heard the oven timer go off.
